newsitem.title: USA: Cook County Ill. to sue tobacco companies for health costs.
newsitem.headline: Cook County Ill. to sue tobacco companies for health costs.

text.p: Officials of Illinois' Cook County, which includes Chicago, announced Wednesday it will sue the tobacco companies for health care costs incurred by uninsured smokers.

The county would become the latest of roughly two dozen local governments across the country to launch suits against cigarette makers in an effort to recoup millions of dollars in taxpayer funds spent to treat smoking-related illnesses.
Cook County prosecutor Richard Devine and county board President John Stroger announced the planned suit at a news conference.

They did not specify whether the suit would be filed in state or federal court, but estimated the county had spent $35 million over 10 years paying hospital costs for uninsured patients' with smoking-related ailments.
Attorneys general of 22 states have sued the tobacco companies and their representatives to recoup Medicaid health care costs related to smoking.

Last week, cigarette manufacturer Liggett Group, which is owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Inc., agreed to a settlement with the states that included turning over documents which could prove damaging to other cigarette manufacturers.
